review.readiness_note: Visual sign-off for the captured 390px viewport. The capture exposes the expected records and entry points, but cannot verify playback, navigation destinations, expanded settings or downstream approval transactions and creator-fee deductions. The document-end tab bar is the stated capture accommodation, not drift.
review.why: The supplied Lab is a desktop Content workspace, so this is a transfer-of-language assessment rather than a one-to-one screen comparison. Production applies that language convincingly: the source stays identifiable, the 12px-lower graphite commitment attaches directly to a cobalt amount, and the remaining records sit on quiet, largely borderless surfaces. At 390px, the source controls, financial facts, submission states and settings disclosure fit without visible clipping or collisions. Financial meaning is consistent: approval triggers payment, $75.00 is stated per approved video, and paid-to-date is separate from current credit. Nothing visible implies escrow, reserved funds or a fee added to the business payment. The review count also agrees with the visible submission states. No actionable implementation drift is evident.
review.verdict: Yes—Frame Shift is faithfully transferred at this phone viewport, with real campaign functionality visibly preserved and no release-blocking visual drift.
